name: Kbd
purpose: Render native keyboard-input notation with finished Brick sizing and visual recipes.
useWhen: Copy needs to name a physical or virtual keyboard key or show a compact authored key sequence.

avoidWhen.condition: The application must register or execute a shortcut.
The content is a technical literal rather than keyboard input.

composition: Keep Kbd inside meaningful surrounding copy or repeat Kbd for each authored key in a sequence with visible separators outside the key hosts.

rules.statement: Preserve the one native kbd host and use it only for keyboard-input notation.
Do not register shortcuts, listen for keys, translate platform labels, or add interaction inside Kbd.
Select only the documented raised, outline, subtle, or plain variant and sm, md, or lg size.
Load styles.css or core.css plus kbd.css.

commonMistakes.mistake: Putting an entire shortcut such as Ctrl+Shift+P inside one Kbd host without authored separation.
commonMistakes.correction: Use one Kbd per key and keep visible separators in the surrounding content owner.

validation: Confirm native kbd semantics, closed recipes, readable key sequences, selection and copy, forced colors, zoom, localization, RTL, and CSS delivery.
Confirm Kbd adds no tab stop, role, shortcut listener, or platform detection.
